subject: language_arts

unit.title: Fluent reading: longer words & expression
unit.essentialQuestion: How do I read big words and long sentences smoothly, like a storyteller?

title: Clap it into beats: reading long words by syllable
objectives: By the end, I can read a long word by chopping it into syllables (beats).

vocabulary.example: rab + bit pushed together makes rabbit

emphasize: A long word is not one scary lump — it is a string of small beats you already know how to read.
The move that must land: clap → read each beat → push together. Repeat the magic phrase: 'Clap it into beats first.'
Pre-empt the misconception that you must read a long word in one go (working-memory overload) — and catch guessing from the first letter instead of reading every beat.

keyConcepts: a syllable is a beat in a word
clap the beats, read each beat, blend the whole word
long words are strings of readable chunks
misconceptions: trying to read a long word in one gulp and stalling (working-memory overload)
guessing a long word from its first letter instead of reading each beat
merging beats when clapping (saying 2 beats for elephant)
hooks: Knock down a scary word like toppling a tower of blocks — one clap per beat.
priorKnowledge: blending sounds in short CVC words like cat (Year 1 Phase 5)

digital: word cards on screen (rabbit, sunset, playground, elephant, picnic, dinosaur, jumper, basket, fantastic)
speak blocks — the tutor listens to the child read aloud

video.title: #BacktoSchool - Introducing: Syllables | Learn to Read | Alphablocks
video.watchTask: Every time the Alphablocks build a word, clap its beats and say them OUT LOUD before the video does.

afterCheck.question: What do we call each beat in a word?

plan.goal: Frame long words as towers to knock down beat by beat; retrieve Year 1 blending with a quick CVC read.
plan.note: Keep the energy playful — the 'knock the tower down' image carries the whole lesson. The warm-up speak block checks blending is secure before we chop anything.
plan.successCriteria: Child reads 'cat' aloud smoothly and is curious about the fantastic trick.

script.say: I've got a word here that looks SO long it might be a bit scary. Ready? FANTASTIC! Whoa. But watch this — I'm going to knock that big word down, one beat at a time, like toppling a tower of blocks. Fan — tas — tic! Want to learn the trick? First, warm up your reading voice. Read this little word for me out loud: cat.
script.adaptHints: If the child loves a building toy or a game with towers, swap 'tower of blocks' for that. If blending 'cat' is shaky, sound it finger by finger — /c/ /a/ /t/ — push together, then do 'sun' before moving on.

blocks.caption: One clap per beat — knock the big word down!

blocks.prompt: Warm up your reading voice — read this little word out loud.

stuckProtocol: If blending is shaky: sound it with the child sound by sound — /c/ /a/ /t/ — then 'push them together: cat.' Do one more, sun, before moving on.

plan.goal: Teach the three magic steps on rabbit: clap the beats, read each beat, push together.
plan.note: The whiteboard shows the dots appearing under each beat as the tutor claps. Say the magic phrase at least twice: 'Clap it into beats first.'
plan.successCriteria: Child can point to the two beats of rabbit and echo the three steps.

script.say: A long word is made of little beats. We call each beat a SYLLABLE. Watch me read rabbit. Step one — I clap the beats: rab (clap!) bit (clap!). Two beats! Step two — I read each beat on its own: /r/ /a/ /b/… rab. /b/ /i/ /t/… bit. Step three — I push them together, faster: rab-bit… rabbit! Three steps every time: clap, read each beat, push together. Clap it into beats first — we never read a long word in one big gulp.
script.adaptHints: Invite the child to clap along on the table or their knees. Match the clap speed to the child's energy.

elements.value: clap · read each beat · push together

blocks.title: The three magic steps
steps: Read each beat on its own
Push them together — read the whole word

plan.goal: Shared beat-reading: sunset (2), playground (2), elephant (3) — the child claps along, then leads on elephant.
plan.note: Tutor claps first, child echoes, then the child leads. The speak block is the child's first solo beat-read — listen for beats, not a one-gulp guess.
plan.successCriteria: Child claps three beats for elephant and reads it beat by beat, then blended.

script.say: Now you clap WITH me. Here's sunset. Clap the beats with me… sun (clap!) set (clap!). Two beats! Read each one… sun… set… push together — sunset! Let's do playground… play (clap!) ground (clap!)… playground! Now the big one — elephant. It's YOUR turn to lead. Clap it, count the beats, then read it to me beat by beat.
script.adaptHints: If the child loves animals, celebrate elephant extra hard. If they merge beats, say it slowly together with a hand under the chin — the jaw drops once per beat.

blocks.prompt: Your turn to lead! Clap the beats, then read this word out loud, beat by beat.

check.question: Clap elephant and tell me how many beats.

wrongAnswers.why: beats ran together
wrongAnswers.remedy: Put a hand under your chin — the jaw drops once per beat. Say it slowly: el… e… phant. How many drops did you feel?

wrongAnswers.answer: tries to read it in one go and stalls
wrongAnswers.why: working-memory overload — too many sounds at once
wrongAnswers.remedy: Clap it into beats first! Clap with me: el (clap) e (clap) phant (clap). Now read just the first beat.

plan.goal: The lesson's key check: count the syllables in elephant AND read it aloud by beats.
plan.note: Both halves matter — the count shows they hear the beats; the read shows they can use them. Probe after success: 'How did you knock it down? Show me the beats.'
plan.successCriteria: Child answers 3 beats and reads el-e-phant → elephant aloud.

script.say: Check time! How many syllables are in elephant? Pick your answer… and then read the whole word to me out loud, beat by beat.
script.adaptHints: After a correct answer, probe: 'How did you knock it down? Show me the beats.'

blocks.prompt: Now read it to me — beat by beat, then push it together.

check.question: How many syllables in elephant — and read it.

wrongAnswers.why: beats run together
wrongAnswers.remedy: Hand under the chin — the jaw drops once per beat. Say it slowly: el… e… phant — feel three drops.

wrongAnswers.answer: reads it in one gulp and stalls
wrongAnswers.why: working-memory overload — trying to hold all the sounds at once
wrongAnswers.remedy: Clap it into beats first. Clap it together, dot each beat, then read one beat at a time.

plan.goal: Independent beat-reading: picnic, dinosaur, jumper, basket — clap, read each beat, blend.
plan.note: Director draws from practiceBank, start level 2, biased towards speak items — this is a reading-aloud lesson. Watch for skipping the clap and guessing from the first letter; remind 'clap first'. Watch for reading beats correctly but forgetting to blend — prompt 'now push them together.'
plan.successCriteria: Child beat-reads at least three long words (one 3-beat) with no one-gulp attempts.

script.say: Practice time, word-toppler! I'll show you words — you clap the beats, read each beat out loud, then push them together and read me the whole word. Ready? Knock them down!
script.adaptHints: Celebrate each toppled word with the tower image. If the child has favourite animals or foods, note that dinosaur and picnic connect nicely — but never change the target words.

stuckProtocol: Name why: 'This one's got lots of beats — let's chop it.'
Drop to concrete: clap it together and dot each beat on the board.
ONE hint: read just the first beat with them.
Re-ask the smaller version: 'read just pic… now just nic' — then blend.
Keep it safe: 'Mistakes show us what to practise. Let's take it one beat at a time.'

plan.goal: Child teaches back the three magic steps; end on process praise and an earned win.
plan.note: Child-led teach-back — the tutor listens. Then the optional Alphablocks syllables video as a reinforcer with the clap-along task.
plan.successCriteria: Child states: clap the beats, read each beat, push together.

script.say: Teach it back to me — if a word looks really long and scary, what are the three magic steps? … Yes! Clap the beats, read each beat, push together. You didn't give up on the big words — you clapped them into beats and knocked them down one at a time. That's exactly what strong readers do.
script.adaptHints: Praise the observed process only — the clapping, the beat-by-beat reading, the not-guessing. If there's time, offer the Alphablocks syllables video with the clap-along task.

block.prompt: Clap the beats, read each beat out loud, then push them together.

practiceBank.expectedAnswer: rab-bit read as two beats, then blended: 'rabbit'

wrongAnswers.answer: guesses a different word from the first letters (e.g. 'rub' or 'ribbon')
wrongAnswers.why: guessing from the first letter instead of reading each beat
wrongAnswers.remedy: Cover everything except 'rab'. Read just that beat… now just 'bit'. Push them together — what word did you build?

wrongAnswers.answer: reads it in one long gulp and stalls
wrongAnswers.why: working-memory overload — too many sounds at once
wrongAnswers.remedy: Clap it into beats first: rab (clap) bit (clap). Now read one beat at a time.

hints: Clap it first — how many beats do you feel?
Read just the first beat: rab. Now the next one.

reteach.say: Let's knock this one down together. Clap with me: rab (clap), bit (clap) — two beats. Read the first beat… rab. The second… bit. Now push them together, faster: rab-bit… rabbit! Two little beats, one big word.

block.caption: rab · bit — two beats make rabbit

block.prompt: Clap it out: how many beats in sunset?

wrongAnswers.why: beats merged into one
wrongAnswers.remedy: Hand under your chin and say it slowly — sun… set. How many times did your jaw drop?

wrongAnswers.why: clapped an extra beat by stretching a sound
wrongAnswers.remedy: Say it at talking speed and clap: sun-set. Each clap is one beat — try again with me.

hints: Say the word and clap along with your voice.
sun… set — one clap for each part.

reteach.say: Beats are the claps hiding inside a word. Say sunset with me and clap: sun (clap), set (clap). Two claps, two beats. Your chin drops once for each beat too — try it with your hand under your chin!

block.prompt: Knock this word down! Clap the beats, read each beat, then read the whole word.

practiceBank.expectedAnswer: pic-nic read beat by beat, then blended: 'picnic'

wrongAnswers.why: read the first letters and guessed instead of finishing the beats
wrongAnswers.remedy: Good start on 'pic' — but there's a whole second beat waiting. Read just 'nic'… now push them together.

wrongAnswers.answer: reads the beats but never blends the word
wrongAnswers.why: forgot step three — push together
wrongAnswers.remedy: You read both beats perfectly! Now say them faster and faster: pic-nic, pic-nic… what word is it?

hints: Read just the first beat, then the second — then push.

reteach.say: Watch me chop it: pic… nic. Two beats. I read the first one — pic. The second — nic. Now the magic push: pic-nic… picnic! A picnic is much friendlier once you've chopped it up.

interestSlots: a picnic with the child's favourite snack

block.prompt: Another tower to topple! Clap the beats, read each one, then the whole word.

practiceBank.expectedAnswer: bas-ket read beat by beat, then blended: 'basket'

wrongAnswers.answer: guesses 'bat' or 'best' from the first letters
wrongAnswers.why: guessing from the first letter instead of reading every beat
wrongAnswers.remedy: Cover the second half. Read just 'bas'… now uncover and read 'ket'. Push them together.

wrongAnswers.answer: reads it in one gulp and stumbles
wrongAnswers.why: one-gulp overload
wrongAnswers.remedy: Clap it into beats first: bas (clap) ket (clap). One beat at a time.

hints: Two claps hide in this word — find them.
bas… then ket — read each, then push together.

reteach.say: Let's chop it together. Bas (clap)… ket (clap). Read with me: bas… ket… bas-ket… basket! See? You already knew how to read both beats — the clap just showed you where to stop.

block.prompt: Clap each word out loud, then sort it by its beats.

practiceBank.expectedAnswer: rabbit and picnic → 2 beats; elephant and dinosaur → 3 beats

wrongAnswers.why: ran el-e together into one beat
wrongAnswers.remedy: Hand under the chin: el… e… phant. Count the jaw drops — how many?

wrongAnswers.why: squashed di-no into one beat
wrongAnswers.remedy: Clap it slowly with me: di (clap) no (clap) saur (clap). How many claps?

hints: Say each word OUT LOUD and clap — don't sort silently.
Your chin drops once per beat — use your hand to count.

reteach.say: The secret is to say the word out loud — beats hide when we read silently. Rabbit: rab-bit, two claps. Elephant: el-e-phant, three claps. Picnic: pic-nic, two. Dinosaur: di-no-saur, three. Clap first, then sort!

block.prompt: This one's a compound tower — clap the beats, read each, then the whole word.

practiceBank.expectedAnswer: play-ground read beat by beat, then blended: 'playground'

wrongAnswers.why: read the first beat then guessed the rest
wrongAnswers.remedy: 'Play' is spot on — now READ the second beat, don't guess it. Cover 'play' and read what's left.

wrongAnswers.why: beats merged
wrongAnswers.remedy: Hand under chin — feel the jaw drop twice: play… ground.

hints: Both beats are words you know — read each one.

reteach.say: Here's a friendly secret: playground is two little words holding hands. Play… ground. Read the first — play. The second — ground. Push together: playground! Some big words are just small words stuck together.

block.prompt: A three-beat tower! Clap the beats, read each one, then roar the whole word.

practiceBank.expectedAnswer: di-no-saur read beat by beat, then blended: 'dinosaur'

wrongAnswers.why: guessed from the first beats instead of reading all three
wrongAnswers.remedy: Two beats down, one to go! Cover di-no and read just the last beat… now push all three together.

wrongAnswers.answer: reads it in one gulp and stalls
wrongAnswers.why: three beats is too much for one gulp
wrongAnswers.remedy: Clap it into beats first: di (clap) no (clap) saur (clap). Read one stepping stone at a time.

hints: Three claps hide in here — find them first.
di… no… then the last beat. One at a time.

reteach.say: Even dinosaur-sized words fall to the three steps. Clap: di (clap) no (clap) saur (clap). Read each beat: di… no… saur. Now push: di-no-saur… dinosaur! You just read a three-beat word — that's expert chopping.

block.prompt: The stretch challenge — a FOUR-beat word! Clap all four beats, read each, then the whole word.

practiceBank.expectedAnswer: cat-er-pil-lar read beat by beat, then blended: 'caterpillar'

wrongAnswers.why: guessing from the first beat
wrongAnswers.remedy: 'Cat' is beat one of FOUR. Read the next beat on its own… and the next. Every beat gets read, none get guessed.

wrongAnswers.answer: reads all four beats but can't blend the whole word
wrongAnswers.why: lost the thread over four beats
wrongAnswers.remedy: Join them two at a time: cat-er… pil-lar… now push the two halves together.

hints: Clap it slowly — four claps hide in there.
Read two beats, then the next two, then join the halves.

reteach.say: Four beats — our biggest tower yet! Watch: cat (clap) er (clap) pil (clap) lar (clap). Read each: cat… er… pil… lar. Now join two at a time: cat-er… pil-lar… caterpillar! Any word, however long, falls to the clap.

block.prompt: The word from the start of the lesson — can you topple it yourself now? Clap, read each beat, push together.

practiceBank.expectedAnswer: fan-tas-tic read beat by beat, then blended: 'fantastic'

wrongAnswers.why: guessed after the first beat
wrongAnswers.remedy: 'Fan' is beat one — now READ beat two on its own. Cover the rest so your eyes stay on one stepping stone.

wrongAnswers.answer: one-gulp attempt that stalls in the middle
wrongAnswers.why: working-memory overload
wrongAnswers.remedy: Clap it into beats first: fan (clap) tas (clap) tic (clap). One beat at a time — you know all three.

hints: This was our scary word — but you know the trick now. Clap first!
fan… tas… tic — read each beat, then push.

reteach.say: Remember when fantastic looked scary? Watch it fall: fan (clap) tas (clap) tic (clap). Read: fan… tas… tic… fantastic! The word that scared us at the start is yours now. That's what the three steps do.

block.caption: fan · tas · tic — you toppled the scary word!

adaptivity.levelUp: 2 consecutive correct at the current level → next level. At level 3, interleave 3- and 4-beat speak items. Prefer speak items throughout — this is a reading-aloud lesson and the tutor should hear the child's voice on most turns.
adaptivity.levelDown: 2 misses on the same skill → run the item's reteach (clap together, dot the beats), then drop one level to a 2-beat word for a guaranteed win.
adaptivity.masterySignal: Child independently beat-reads 3+ words including one 3-beat word, using clap → read beats → blend with no one-gulp attempts → mastery ≥ 0.8 for 'reading long words by syllable'.
struggleProtocol: Name why: 'This one's got lots of beats — let's chop it.'
Drop to concrete: clap it together and dot each beat.
ONE hint: read just the first beat with them.
Re-ask the smaller version: one beat at a time, then blend.
Keep it safe: 'Mistakes show us what to practise. One beat at a time.'
adaptivity.personalization: Swap the 'tower of blocks' frame for a construction toy or game the child loves. Celebrate dinosaur/animal words if the child is an animal fan. Never change the target words — the syllable work is the lesson.
adaptivity.endOnSuccess: Finish on a word the child can topple (drop to a 2-beat word if needed) and praise the process: 'you clapped it into beats and read every single one — no guessing.'

differentiation.support: Tutor claps the beats first; child echoes the claps, then reads each beat. Use 2-beat words only (rabbit, sunset, picnic, jumper, basket) for a guaranteed win before any 3-beat word.
differentiation.stretch: Chop a 4-beat word — caterpillar (cat-er-pil-lar) — clapping and reading all four beats.

extension: Hunt for the longest word on a page of a favourite book and beat-read it out loud to the tutor.
assessmentEvidence: Child independently claps and reads at least two long words (one 3-beat) using clap → read beats → blend, with no one-gulp attempts.
revisitLater: Bring back elephant and picnic as a 30-second warm-up at the start of Lesson 2, and again in Lesson 4's Robot vs Storyteller review.
